Apple and indie teams conflate four authentication stories under Sign-In & Security. AppLocale covers Apple Recovery Key listing metadata — the 28-character user-generated recovery key — not the sibling features:

  • Apple Recovery Key (this page) — user-generated 28-character Apple Account recovery key under Settings → Sign-In & Security → Recovery Key; restores access when trusted devices and verification codes are unavailable.   • Security Keys (different, sibling under 2FA) — physical FIDO2 hardware registered under Sign-In & Security → Two-Factor Authentication → Security Keys; tap a YubiKey or Titan key instead of a verification code — 安全密钥 vocabulary. Covered on our Security Keys guide — hardware FIDO keys, not 恢复密钥.
  • Passkeys (different) — passwordless credentials saved in iCloud Keychain; Sign in with a passkey and Create a passkey marketing. Covered on our Passkeys guide — not Apple Account Recovery Key enrollment.
  • Account Recovery Contacts (different) — trusted contacts who can help recover a locked Apple Account — separate listing story we do not cover on this page. Do not create Legacy Contact or Safety Check pages here.
  • Sign in with Apple (different) — Continue with Apple and Hide My Email login badges for third-party apps. Covered on our Sign in with Apple guide — not Apple Account Recovery Key enrollment.

Your gallery may show a Recovery Key generation walkthrough on one frame and an in-app security dashboard on the next — but listing copy should name each claim accurately per frame. A Recovery Key badge is not a verification-code entry sheet, not an Add Security Key hardware registration flow, not a passkey creation sheet, and not a Sign in with Apple button unless that is what the screenshot shows.

What Apple Recovery Key actually does — listing honesty

Apple Recovery Key is a user-generated 28-character key for the Apple Account. Under Settings → [your name] → Sign-In & Security → Recovery Key, buyers create a key they must store safely — then if they lose all trusted devices and cannot receive verification codes, the Recovery Key can restore Apple Account access. Third-party apps may complement this by educating buyers, documenting key-storage best practices, or aligning security UX with account-recovery workflows. Recovery Key–specific vocabulary — what translates differently in zh-Hans

Account-recovery marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general localization guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers evaluate Apple Recovery Key — not a literal paste of US marketing:

设置 → [你的姓名] → 登录与安全性 → 恢复密钥

Apple's Chinese Settings path is 设置 → [你的姓名] → 登录与安全性 → 恢复密钥. Screenshot walkthroughs and caption lines should mirror that path — not English "Sign-In & Security" badges alone, not 面容 ID 与密码 (Stolen Device Protection), and not iCloud (Advanced Data Protection). AppLocale uses the labels buyers see on a zh-Hans iPhone when your English gallery shows the Recovery Key toggle or 28-character key generation sheet.

恢复密钥 (Recovery Key)

Apple's official zh-Hans label for the 28-character Apple Account recovery key is 恢复密钥. Commerce copy may also use 帐户恢复密钥 or 账户恢复密钥 when buyers search those terms — but do not substitute literal 恢复键, which reads like machine translation and does not match Apple's Settings UI. Never substitute 安全密钥 — that is Security Keys (FIDO hardware), not Recovery Key.

28 位恢复密钥 (28-character key)

US pages use "28-character key" or "28-character Recovery Key." China storefront copy uses 28 位恢复密钥 on frames that show the key-generation sheet. Do not substitute 验证码 (verification code) or 通行密钥 (Passkeys) vocabulary unless the screenshot shows those features.

生成恢复密钥 (Generate Recovery Key)

When your English subtitle or description says "Generate your Recovery Key" as part of Apple Account recovery setup, zh-Hans buyers expect 生成恢复密钥 or 创建恢复密钥 on enrollment walkthrough frames. Do not substitute 开启双重认证 (Turn On Two-Factor Authentication), 添加安全密钥 (Add Security Key), or 创建通行密钥 (Create a passkey) — those belong on sibling pages.

安全存储恢复密钥 (Store your recovery key safely)

US pages use "Store your Recovery Key safely" or "Save your account recovery key offline." China marketing uses 安全存储恢复密钥 or 离线保存恢复密钥 on key-storage education frames. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual scope — listing copy about why buyers should store keys, not implying AppLocale or your app holds buyer Recovery Keys.

  • Leaving "Recovery Key" untranslated — Apple and buyers expect 恢复密钥 in zh-Hans regions; English-only overlay lines on otherwise Chinese copy looks unfinished
  • Using literal 恢复键 — machine-translation phrasing that does not match Apple's official 恢复密钥 Settings label
  • Conflating 恢复密钥 with 安全密钥 — 安全密钥 and 添加安全密钥 belong on the Security Keys guide; the 28-character Recovery Key is this page — never mix the two on one caption line
  • Conflating Recovery Key with Two-Factor Authentication — 双重认证, 验证码, and 受信设备 belong on the Two-Factor Authentication guide; Recovery Key is the offline 28-character backup when 2FA devices fail
  • Conflating Recovery Key with Passkeys — 通行密钥 and 无密码登录 belong on the Passkeys guide; Recovery Key is account recovery under Sign-In & Security

  • Conflating Recovery Key with Advanced Data Protection — ADP may require a Recovery Key to enable iCloud encryption, but ADP marketing is a separate lead story; see Advanced Data Protection listing when iCloud end-to-end encryption is your hero
  • Overpromising account recovery outcomes — honest copy describes what your app does when buyers create Recovery Keys on their Apple Account; we do not guarantee buyers avoid account lockouts
  • Assuming Recovery Key education localizes the store page — in-app content and App Store metadata are independent workstreams
